<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json abc25a3536e2f00cc55ee6745320cb8f7209c459` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `678e84ab87abd237a624fc971c816db82ce4b59b` — the merge of head `c0fb1c715f485d6f58a6eaf5ec5363db054c97c4` into base `abc25a3536e2f00cc55ee6745320cb8f7209c459`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 678e84ab87abd237a624fc971c816db82ce4b59b && git checkout 678e84ab87abd237a624fc971c816db82ce4b59b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin abc25a3536e2f00cc55ee6745320cb8f7209c459 c0fb1c715f485d6f58a6eaf5ec5363db054c97c4 && git checkout -B drift-repro abc25a3536e2f00cc55ee6745320cb8f7209c459 && git merge --no-ff c0fb1c715f485d6f58a6eaf5ec5363db054c97c4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json abc25a3536e2f00cc55ee6745320cb8f7209c459
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs abc25a3536e2f00cc55ee6745320cb8f7209c459` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d19b65bf1c98b3cb282ab85007fd8bb36a4680f8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data-write-request-gate.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-object-discovery.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`getMetaItems` / `readFlattenedMetaItems`, `getMetaItem` / `getMetaItemForExecution` / `readMetaItemFace`, `assertObjectRegistered`, `objectPackageDisabledError`), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`objectItemReader`, `enforceApiAccess`, `metaListSource`), packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (`loadObjectItem`), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`resolveService`), packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts (the `GET /meta/:type` list branch, `answerMetaList`), packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts (the `/data` door's gate calls), packages/runtime/src/api-exposure.ts (`checkApiExposure`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`getObject`, `isPackageDisabled`, `isObjectPackageDisabled`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`aggregate`), packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts (`list_objects`, `describe_object`, `validate_expression`)

Inputs: card #25120 (body, claim 6322493221, report 6324844375, takeover claim 6327821572), PR #25136 (body, five-file list, net diff against `main` at the head above), and the 41 check-runs on that head: 34 `success`, 7 `skipped` by design, 0 `failure`; the five required contexts (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard) are `success`. No governed surface is in the file list. The face is the changeset's and the PR body's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Discovery reads the protocol's merged listing — RIGHT.** `readMergedItems` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts:454-471`) is the one unwrap of `getMetaItems`, shared by the skill read and the object reads; `getProtocol` (`:572`) resolves `protocol` per request through the same `deps.resolveService(context, name, envId)` chain `getMeta` uses, the seam the skill read has used since commit e783e163d. `listObjectSummaries` (`:602-614`) and `describeObject` (`:661-678`) answer from that listing; the dispatcher's own `GET /meta/:type` calls the same `protocol.getMetaItems({ type })` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts:2211`) and `RestServer`'s list source does too (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:3578-3588`), and `readFlattenedMetaItems` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:10058` onward) reads this kernel's own registry and omits a disabled package's items by the one predicate `isItemOfDisabledPackage` (`:553-555`). So list membership equals what `GET /api/v1/meta/object` serves the same caller: the per-caller work `answerMetaList` adds (`domains/meta.ts:619-656`) is a field projection of each object, not a membership filter, and the new pin measures the equality in-process on every shape. `sys_` objects stay filtered by the tool (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts:286-288`, `:706-708`). The three outcomes are the skill read's: structural absence keeps the `metadata` service read; a throw travels to the client (contract item 8), the direction `domains/meta.ts:2215-2230` takes for REST. `listObjectsDiagnosed` (`mcp.ts:640-655`) keeps the `metadata` service's `listDiagnosed('object')` verdict; the protocol has no diagnosed list read and `getMetaItems` throws rather than shorting on a store outage, so that verdict is the only completeness signal the host has — right, as the card asked. Not new, not a blocker: `describeObject` serves the raw `fields` map where REST's list projects fields per caller — exactly what the old `getObject` read served — and it reads the whole served listing (with `_diagnostics` computed per object) on every call where the served by-name face would read one object; a cost, not a contract change.

2. **The gate's healthy by-name read — RIGHT.** `readExposureDeclaration` (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:336-359`) asks `getMetaItemForExecution`, else `getMetaItem`, byte for byte `RestServer.objectItemReader` (`rest-server.ts:2555-2557`), and accepts the item only under its own name, the rule `loadObjectItem` applies (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:492-497`). `readMetaItemFace` (`protocol.ts:11440-11455`) shares every source, merge and the disabled-package refusal between the two faces and skips only the serving decorations; the gate reads `enable` and serves no byte, so the execution face is the one `getMetaItemForExecution`'s docblock licenses. The registry resolves short names and legacy FQNs (`registry.ts:4575`, `:5853`), so an item resolved under another name is "no declaration" on this door exactly as on REST's: shared, pre-existing, not widened here. `String(object)` changes nothing.

3. **The outage fallback keeps the old refusal set as a floor — RIGHT.** Any throw but `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` reads the `metadata` service's copy (`action-execution.ts:356`), the source this gate read on every input before the move, and the outer fail-open `catch` (`:399-400`) is unchanged, so no input is more exposed during an outage than it was on every request before. `loadObjectItem` fails open on the same throw (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:501-506`), so this door is at most REST's exposure then. Noted, not blocking: REST logs that fall-open; the runtime fallback is silent, as the old `catch` was.

4. **`OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` read as "no declaration" — WRONG on one door, and it WIDENS.** `action-execution.ts:355` adopts `loadObjectItem`'s reading (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:500`) on the premise the PR states in its docblock and in contract item 6: "the data plane then refuses the request with that same code". That premise holds on REST and on five of `callData`'s six arms: `findData`, `getData`, `createData`, `updateData` and `deleteData` each run `assertObjectRegistered` (`protocol.ts:14526`, `:15162`, `:15254`, `:15399`, `:15523`), which throws `objectPackageDisabledError` for an object of a disabled package (`:12921-12922`, constructor `:518-527`). It does NOT hold on the `aggregate` arm: `callData` (`action-execution.ts:674-706`) takes no protocol there by design and calls `engine.aggregate` directly, the engine resolves the object through `registry.getObject` (`engine.ts:21468` onward), the registry serves a disabled package's objects on purpose (`registry.ts:5826-5856`), and no site in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` asks `isObjectPackageDisabled`. Consequence, on exactly the input the review was asked to probe: a disabled package's object declared `enable.apiEnabled: false`, on any kernel where the `metadata` service holds its copy (every kernel without an `environmentId`, and any kernel after a marketplace install — the PR's own table rows 2 to 4, and the shape its disabled-package pin boots). Before this diff `aggregate_records` on it was refused `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED` from the copy; on this head `readExposureDeclaration` turns the protocol's refusal into `undefined`, `checkApiExposure(undefined, 'aggregate')` allows (`packages/runtime/src/api-exposure.ts:119`), and `engine.aggregate` serves grouped rows of an object the author declared off the API and the operator switched off. One refusal removed on the narrowing face; the PR's contract item 6 ("every data verb ... `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, the status does not move") and the changeset's "Also changed" sentence are false for `aggregate_records`. The pins do not reach it: the disabled-package block (`mcp-package-object-discovery.test.ts:323-354`) pins listing and describe only, and no `DATA_VERBS` row (`:220-227`) runs against `qa_off_gated`. Fix, small and REST-parity-preserving: a refused `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` is a refusal, not an outage and not an absence — rethrow it from `readExposureDeclaration` past `refuseUnexposedDataAction`'s fail-open `catch` (`:398-401`; it already carries the ADR-0112 `code`, `status` and `object` the data door throws), so every arm answers `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` whether or not it reaches the protocol; then add the six `DATA_VERBS` rows to the disabled-package block expecting `{ code: 'OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED', status: 404 }` with the store spies never called, and re-measure the gate ablation against them. Asking the registry's `isObjectPackageDisabled` on the aggregate arm alone would close the same hole but leaves the gate's answer door-dependent.

5. **The dispatcher's `/data` door and the hono catch-all narrow identically — RIGHT.** `domains/data.ts:237`, `:338`, `:455` ask the same gate; no `/data` route reaches `callData('aggregate')`, so judgment 4 is the `/mcp` `aggregate_records` tool (and any future `callData('aggregate')` caller).

6. **Multi-environment host — RIGHT, parity.** On a kernel-resolver host the request's own kernel answers first (`http-dispatcher.ts:2576-2583`), so each environment's bridge reads its own registry, pinned by the two-environment block (`mcp-package-object-discovery.test.ts:356-407`); on a SharedProjectPlugin host the chain is the one `metadata` already takes, so no environment is more exposed than its `metadata` read was.

7. **Rig re-judge — RIGHT.** `stubObjectReads` (`data-write-request-gate.test.ts:168-181`) answers `getMetaItems` and both by-name faces from the registry; the dispatcher door is given no `metadata` service (`:289`), so a gate that stopped reading the protocol has nothing to fall back to and reds — the shape a healthy-path rig owes.

8. **Public surface — RIGHT, none moves.** `McpMergedMetadataRead` was already exported; `readMergedItems`, `readExposureDeclaration` and `ExposureDeclarationRead` are module-private; `packages/mcp` and `packages/spec` are untouched; the `metadata` service gets no second copy, as the card required.

Verdict on the face: judgments 1 to 3 and 5 to 8 narrow or hold; judgment 4 widens one input class, so this head is not the narrowing its `Clause-②` line declares.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/runtime': patch` with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` in the changeset body; `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (no authorable key, accepted value or default moves — an `enable.apiEnabled` the author already wrote is enforced where it was not read). A non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition, so the level is right, and `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` ran green inside Lint & Repo Gates on this head. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right arm for the intended change, but judgment 4 makes it untrue of this head until closed; the fix does not move the level (still `patch`, still breaking, still `none`).

### ③ Boundary flags

Report comment 6324844375: `open_questions` is empty — nothing to answer.

`deviations`, each judged:
1. The gate reads the by-name face rather than `getMetaItems` — right (REST parity; no per-request whole-list diagnostic pass).
2. Outage fallback to the copy, plus a fourth pin — the fallback is right as a floor (judgment 3); the fourth pin covers contract item 5 only, and item 6 is unpinned and false on `aggregate_records` (judgment 4).
3. Fixture re-judged — right (judgment 7).
4. `origin/main` merged before the PR — fine; the check-runs above are on the merged head.
5. Model-free commit trailers and the session-URL PR footer — matches AGENTS.md.
6. The ADR-0087 marker as an HTML comment in the changeset file — that is the form its gate reads; fine.

`out_of_scope_findings`, each answered or escalated:
1. `list_actions` / `run_action` read `metadata.listObjects()` (`collectActionDeclarations`) — same family, measured by the dev. ESCALATED: the seat files it from the report's evidence and dedupe words. Not a blocker here.
2. The stdio half (`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`) measures the same defect — held off by the dispatch. ESCALATED: the seat files it; its fix must not copy judgment 4's reading as it stands.
3. The `GATED_ACTIONS` docblock in `packages/mcp` now misdescribes the HTTP bridge's object read — under the same hold-off; rides on finding 2's card. Noted.
4. Card acceptance item 3 (walked on a cloud environment with a marketplace app) NOT MEASURED — the cloud host is outside this repo. The PR body says `Fixes #25120`, which closes the card on merge with that item unmeasured. ESCALATED: the seat decides whether the card closes on this PR or stays open for the cloud walk.
5. New, from this review: `callData`'s aggregate arm never asks the data plane's `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` gate, so `aggregate_records` on a disabled package's `apiEnabled: true` object was served before this PR and still is — pre-existing, not widened here; the seat files it, and the rethrow in judgment 4 closes it in passing.
6. Noted, not blocking: `describe_object` field visibility versus REST's per-caller projection (judgment 1) — pre-existing.

What a PASS on the next head needs: judgment 4 closed (the gate rethrows `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, or the aggregate arm asks the registry), the six data-verb rows pinned on the disabled package's gated object with the store spies, the gate ablation re-measured against them, and the contract item 6 claim then true on every verb.
